# Tua language contract for models

Tua is Lua first: a gradual typed superset that emits readable Lua
5.1-compatible code for LuaJIT and LOVE 11.x. Write normal Lua unless a Tua
addition supplies useful static information or nearby source already uses it.
Never answer with TypeScript, JavaScript, Luau, Python, or Markdown.

## Completion policy

- Continue the syntax and style around the cursor. Output only the inserted
  source: no explanation, fence, suffix repetition, or unrelated rewrite.
- Prefer Lua control flow, tables, functions, closures, varargs, metatables,
  `require`, standard globals, and `math`, `string`, and `table` libraries.
- Locals infer one stable widened type from a known initializer. Prefer
  `local score = 0` and `local image = love.graphics.newImage(path)`, not
  redundant forms such as `local score: number = 0`.
- Annotate a local only when the annotation adds information: for example
  `local value: number | nil = nil`, `local names: string[] = {}`, an explicit
  `any` boundary, or a wider/public shape not established by the initializer.
- Function, callback, and module boundaries benefit from parameter and return
  annotations, but normal unannotated Lua functions and inferred returns work.
- Prefer visible bindings, existing modules/helpers, and project-native APIs.
  Keep expression and statement completions short and syntactically local.
  When the cursor is in an unfinished function or method, complete its useful
  remaining body and required closing `end` or `}` without repeating suffix
  code.
- Feature index: Lua/LuaJIT syntax and libraries; gradual inference and `any`;
  aliases, shapes, optional fields, arrays, dictionaries, unions,
  literals, enums, function types, defaults, varargs, multiple returns, and
  runtime `is`; compound assignment (names, fields, and indexed targets with
  single evaluation of receiver/key); metatable-style classes and inheritance;
  mixed Lua/Tua modules, static imports, type-only modules, generated modules,
  and LuaDoc; the LOVE 11.x catalog, callbacks, objects, and assets; `Vec2`,
  asset helpers, sprite sheets, Signals, stores, state machines, Baton input,
  object pools, ECS, behavior trees, tweening, camera, procedural helpers,
  and audio systems.

## Lua and modules

- Normal Lua assignments and multiple returns, `nil`, truthiness, tables,
  numeric/generic `for`, `while`, `repeat`/`until`, `if`/`elseif`/`else`,
  local/global functions, colon methods, closures, varargs, and metatables are
  the runtime foundation. Blocks use `then`, `do`, and `end`.
- `require("module")` keeps Lua semantics. Mixed `.lua`/`.tua` projects,
  simple Lua module exports, and LuaDoc/LuaCATS annotations interoperate.
- Static top-level local bindings may use `import("./child")` or
  `import("project.module")`; these lower to `require` and are not JavaScript
  imports. Tua has no JavaScript-style runtime `export`.
- `export type Name = ...` publishes a type alias. Consume exported aliases
  with `import type Types from "./types"` or
  `import type { Player, Room as LevelRoom } from "./types"`; type imports and
  `export type { Player as Hero } from "./types"` re-exports are erased and do
  not load a runtime module. Only explicitly exported aliases cross modules.
  Editor type completion and unknown-type quick fixes can add or extend these
  imports automatically.
- Put declaration-only project modules in `.d.tua` files. They accept type
  aliases, type imports, type exports, and comments, reject runtime statements,
  and never emit Lua or source maps.
- Put `--!tua generated` in the first eight lines of a generated `.tua` module
  when its executable source is Lua 5.1-compatible and its large tables are
  described by LuaDoc schemas. The directive keeps Tua module identity and
  checks entries contextually; it does not make tables immutable.
- LuaDoc support includes `---@class`, `---@field`, `---@alias`, `---@type`,
  `---@param`, `---@return`, `---@overload`, and `---@vararg`, including
  declaration-only external type libraries.
- Statically visible Lua metatable patterns can type `__index`, constructor
  prototypes, `__newindex`, arithmetic/comparison/length/call metamethods,
  `__pairs`, `__ipairs`, and `tostring`; dynamic mutation stays conservative.
- Unknown modules, keys, and metatable behavior stay dynamic through `any`;
  never invent types for runtime-computed Lua.

## LOVE 11.x foundation

- In game code, suggest suitable `love.*` callbacks, modules, constructors,
  enums, and methods rather than browser or Node APIs.
- Callbacks are Lua functions such as `function love.load() ... end`,
  `function love.update(dt) ... end`, `function love.draw() ... end`, and
  `function love.keypressed(key) ... end`; unused parameters may be omitted.
- Native loaders include `love.graphics.newImage`, `newFont`, `newShader`,
  `newCanvas`, `newQuad`, `newSpriteBatch`, `newParticleSystem`,
  `love.image.newImageData`, and `love.audio.newSource`.
- LOVE object methods require colon calls, for example
  `image:setFilter("nearest")`, `image:getWidth()`, and `source:play()`.
- The LOVE catalog supplies callbacks, overloads, enums, object inheritance,
  parameter names, returns, and documentation. Known explicit annotations
  should agree with it.
- Native loader and helper asset paths receive project-aware completion,
  validation, metadata, definition, and references.

## Projects and generated assets

- A `tua.toml` project normally reads sources below `source`, emits Lua below
  `out`, and may index declaration-only external `type_libraries`.
- Opt-in `[[asset_pipelines]]` run before `check`, `build`, and `watch`. Each
  external `command` or built-in importer owns one generated directory below
  the source root and declares regular-file outputs through a version-1 JSON
  manifest. Generated `.tua`, `.d.tua`, Lua, and assets then join the normal
  project flow.
- Asset pipeline commands are trusted local code, not compiler plugins or a
  sandbox. Never invent or enable an importer implicitly. The language server
  only indexes already-materialized output and does not execute pipelines.

## Tua types and syntax

- Primitive types are `number`, `string`, `boolean`, `nil`, and `any`.
  Annotations use `name: Type`; function returns use `): Type`.
- `type Name = ...` declares an erased alias; `type Box<T> = ...` declares a
  generic alias. Apply aliases explicitly in type positions, such as
  `Box<number>`; named and namespace type imports and type re-exports preserve
  the alias. Generic arguments and declarations erase from Lua.
- Shapes use `{ field: Type, optional?: Type }`; arrays use `T[]`;
  dictionaries use `{ [Key]: Value }`; native fixed-length positional table
  types are not supported (`[First, Second]` is LuaCATS-only); unions use
  `A | B`; exact strings use literal types such as
  `"idle" | "running"`.
- `enum Name ... end` is erased string-union sugar.
- Function types use `(value: T) -> U`; parenthesized returns represent
  multiple returns. Declarations support typed `...: Type`, optional trailing
  `mode?: string`, and defaults such as `amount: number = 5`.
- `value is Type` performs supported runtime identity checks and branch
  narrowing. Generic aliases, free functions, and classes support binders;
  free functions and class constructors infer arguments from direct calls.
  Generic classes can extend an applied generic parent and can be shared
  through exported generic instance aliases. A generic parameter may have
  one protocol bound such as `T: Updatable`; generic methods, generic
  protocols, and explicit call-site type arguments remain unsupported.
  Unbounded LuaDoc `---@generic T` binds documented function parameters and
  returns. Tua has no built-in `Table<T>` container; use `T[]` or
  `{ [Key]: Value }` for collections.
- Ordinary functions remain Lua:
  `function name(args): Return ... end` and
  `local function name(args): Return ... end`.
- `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, and `%=` work on names, field chains, and indexed
  targets such as `items[nextIndex()].age`. Indexed receivers and keys evaluate
  once; lowering uses scoped Lua 5.1 locals without wrapping the RHS in a function.
- Classes use `class Name { ... }`, `open class Base { ... }`, or
  `final class Child extends Base { ... }`. Bodies support typed fields and
  defaults, `init(...) { ... }`, methods `name(args): Return { ... }`,
  `override`, final methods, `super(...)`, inheritance, and typed `self`.
  Classes are closed/final by default and construct with `Name.new(...)`.
  Method-only `protocol Name { ... }` contracts can be implemented explicitly
  with `implements`; protocol contracts and type-only imports are erased.
- Class/method bodies close with `}`; Lua functions and control flow close
  with `end`. Types, enums, classes, imports, defaults, `is`, and compound
  assignments lower to LuaJIT-compatible Lua and add no new VM.

## Tua LOVE and game helpers

- `math` and `love.math` provide opt-in `tau`, `clamp`, `lerp`, `inverseLerp`,
  `remap`, `sign`, `round`, `smoothstep`, `rgb`, and `rgba` helpers. `rgb` and
  `rgba` convert 0-255 components into array-like 0-1 color tables. Each helper
  is emitted only in files that reference it.
- Typed asset helpers lower to native LOVE: `image "path"`, `sound "path"`,
  `music "path"`, `font(path, size)`, `shader "path"`, `imageData "path"`,
  `canvas(width, height)`, `quad(...)`, `spriteBatch(image, count)`, and
  `particles(image, count)`.
- `Vec2`/`vec2(x, y)` provide typed BrineVector operations; typed arithmetic
  fuses temporary vectors, including values inferred from required modules.
  Use `v.length`, not `#v`: with the JIT off, vectors are plain tables and
  `#v` returns 0 (lint `TL4060`).
- `spriteSheet({...})` derives exact animation keys and typed `SpriteAnimation`
  values, supports ordered multi-row ranges, registration origins,
  durations/fps, per-animation frames, markers, and loop callbacks.
- `sheet:player(name)` returns a replaceable-runtime `SpritePlayer` with checked
  `play`, `gotoAndPlay`, `gotoAndStop`, marker subscriptions, time updates,
  manual seeking, origin-aware drawing, and explicit leaf insertion into a
  caller-owned `SpriteBatch` through `addToBatch`. Players share the sheet's
  read-only frame, duration, and interval arrays; use `player.speed` for
  per-player timing, or `player.animations.run = player.animations.run:clone()`
  followed by `player:play("run", true)` for private arrays.
- Sprite sheets may contain optional named child sheets; `player:child(name)`
  checks the child name and returns its recursively updated/drawn controller.
- `signal()` provides typed event names/payloads through `on`, `once`,
  `declare`, `emit`, `off`, `clear`, `has`, and `listeners`. Remove a `once`
  handler with the value `once` returns. `onPattern`, `emitPattern`,
  `offPattern`, and `clearPattern` match only event names that already have
  handlers.
- `store({...})` infers state for `get`, `set`, `update`, `subscribe`, and
  typed field `watch`. Its `revision()` advances on every `set` and `update`.
- `Save.contract({slot, version, schema})` declares a bounded JSON snapshot
  with `Save.record`, `array`, `number`, `string`, `boolean`, `optional`, and
  `enum`. Optional `migration_schemas` validate old payloads and pass marker-free
  copies to their matching direct migrations; omitted entries retain `old: any`.
  `load` reports recovery issues; `save` checkpoints explicitly;
  `bind(store, {select, debounce, max_interval})` polls store revisions and
  schedules writes. In `.tua`, `Save` imports its runtime only when referenced.
- `stateMachine({...})` derives state/event names, event methods, transition
  checks, and lifecycle callbacks.
- `input({...})` provides Baton-backed controls/pairs, LOVE key/gamepad source
  completion, polling, deadzones, and joystick support.
- `objectPool({...})` types factory results and supports `acquire`, `release`,
  `prewarm`, ownership/count inspection, cleanup, and `clear`.
- Built-in `ECS` supplies typed components, worlds, systems, and queries
  without an explicit package import. `world:reader(Component)` binds a typed
  entity-ID lookup returning the current payload or nil; readers survive world
  clear/repopulation. `BehaviorTree.new(...)` supplies
  composable actions, conditions, selectors, sequences, and per-actor runners;
  it can be used from ECS systems without creating a tree per entity or frame.
  Annotate a leaf's actor parameter to carry its context through combinators,
  `new(root)`, and `instance(actor)`, including module exports. ECS schema fields
  can name actor/runner aliases. Context-free waits compose with typed leaves;
  incompatible actor contracts fail. Empty `new()` plus later `setRoot` and
  extracted constructor functions retain dynamic context typing.
- Built-in `Tween` animates numeric fields; `Camera.new(...)` follows and
  transforms a game view; `Rot` provides seeded randomness, maps, paths,
  visibility, noise, colors, grammars, and lighting. These names need no
  explicit `require` in `.tua` source. Use PascalCase for built-in module
  values, `ECS` for the acronym, and lower camel case for factory functions
  such as `vec2(...)`, `signal(...)`, and `store(...)`. Existing `ecs` and
  `tween` module spellings remain compatible.
- `Rot.Rng.new(seed)` keeps its legacy seeded sequence. For separate named
  streams use `Rot.Rng.stream(seed, "weapon-rewards")`; names are stable,
  case-sensitive bytes, and seeds must be safe finite integers. Each call returns
  a fresh generator without advancing any other stream. `rng:choice(T[])` returns
  an existing `T` (empty input errors); `rng:shuffle(T[])` returns a fresh shallow
  `T[]`. Typed array elements remain typed through these methods. Named streams
  are deterministic, not cryptographic or guaranteed disjoint.
- `audioSystem({...})` derives exact bus, cue, music-scene, layer, effect, and
  event names. It supports bounded polyphonic voices, priorities, fades,
  snapshots, positional sources, effects, and beat/bar-quantized music; use
  configured names instead of inventing string identifiers.
- Cached audio metadata may come from an `audio-analysis` asset pipeline and a
  generated catalog passed as `analysis`. Authored `bpm`, `offset`, and
  `signature` remain authoritative; analysis is advisory, and dynamic
  `requestAnalysis` is explicit rather than automatic.
- `AudioDesign.render({...})` makes a short setup-time `Source` from a typed
  waveform and envelope; it is not a per-frame synthesizer.
- Built-in helper runtimes are emitted and copied only when referenced. A
  project-provided compatible module can replace a bundled runtime; ordinary
  Lua/LOVE code has no Tua runtime dependency. Static editor previews show
  source-derived declarations, while the opt-in runtime inspector shows sampled
  live state. Do not describe a static graph as a live game trace.
- Use native LOVE freely. Use a Tua helper when nearby code uses it or its
  typed configuration fits the task; do not force helpers into ordinary LOVE.
- Plain `.lua` files access bundled Tua runtimes through explicit imports such
  as `require("tuastore")`, `require("brinevector")`,
  `require("tuaobjectpool")`, `require("tuaaudio")`,
  `require("tuastatemachine").create`, and `require("baton").new`. Literal
  runtime imports are typed and make `tua build` emit the required runtime;
  compiler-only helpers and syntax remain `.tua`-only.

## Never emit

- JavaScript/TypeScript: `const`, `let`, `=>`, `interface`, `namespace`,
  `null`, `undefined`, `this.`, `console.*`, `===`, `!==`, `?.`, `??`,
  JavaScript objects, or `}` to close a Lua function.
- Luau-only casts (`value :: Type`), `continue`, conditional expressions,
  interpolated strings, or Luau generics.
- Invented package managers, runtime type objects, decorators, async/promises,
  DOM APIs, or executable plugins.

- `BoundedQueue` is an opt-in typed bounded FIFO builtin. Use
  `BoundedQueue.new(capacity, typedInitialArray)` with dot methods `push`, `pop`,
  `count`, `capacity`, `rejected`, `clear`, and `drain(limit, visitor)`.
  `push` returns false when full; `pop` returns the payload or nil. Nil
  payloads are forbidden, false is valid. Drains defer new entries, return
  zero when nested, and stop on clear; callbacks must not yield.

- `Readonly<T>` is a built-in deep read-only view of records and collections.
  Mutable inputs are accepted; nested reads/iteration retain read-only payload
  types. Writes, standard table mutation, and mutable parameter escapes fail.
  It erases without copies or freezing mutable aliases; `any` and untyped Lua
  are trust boundaries. Keep explicit copies for time-isolated snapshots.

Dialogue (development, release after 0.11.0): `.tdialogue` scripts under the
source directory compile to typed Lua data modules during check/build/watch.
Use `local document = require("scenes.intro")` for `scenes/intro.tdialogue`, then
`Dialogue.new(document)`. Both `Dialogue` and `BoundedQueue` automatically inject
their runtime imports only when referenced; local bindings take precedence.
Explicit `require("tuadialogue")` / `require("tuaboundedqueue")` remain supported.
The host owns rendering, input and timing. Text IDs must be project-unique.
Share characters using ordinary .tua exports with a required string `name` field.
Before labels, `@characters Cast "dialogue.characters"` imports the module; use
`Cast.Guide: Hello (end)` as a speaker line. Script completion after `Cast.`, hover,
definition navigation and unsaved edits are supported by the updated extension.
Character fields other than name/portrait/nameKey remain host metadata. Analysis
never executes project modules; emitted scripts use ordinary runtime require.
Dialogue localization: `Dialogue.new(document, {locale = "fr", resolve = I18n.dialogue,
args = {name = "Ada", count = 2}})` uses existing configured catalogs and source fallback.
`%{name}` placeholders take scalar args, `%%` escapes a percent; inserted values are literal.
`I18n.dialogueTemplate(key, source, args, locale)` returns an owned record with unexpanded
`template`, optional actual catalog `locale`, and optional actual plural `variant`.
It reuses dialogue catalog/placeholder validation, requires finite count for plurals,
and does not change global locale. Source fallback has no locale/variant. Non-count
args need not be supplied until expansion. This record-returning selector is not a
replacement for the string-returning `resolve` callback. Use it as `resolveTemplate`
for schema-8 rich fields; plain fields/names continue to use `resolve`.
Line text IDs and reply IDs are catalog keys; optional character `nameKey` localizes its name.
`player:setLocale("en")` refreshes presentation without changing visit/generation or replaying events.
Renderers honor `presentationRevision` and `revealComplete` (show refreshed lines fully).
Context-free compiled documents have schemaVersion 1 and line textId; optional `@document logical.id`
before labels supplies documentId. Legacy structured documents remain playable.
Use `assert(Dialogue.schemaVersion >= 1)` when relying on this API with runtime replacements.
`tua dialogue-extract` prints a read-only source-text JSON manifest, never overwrites catalogs.
Localization Explorer includes dialogue coverage/source navigation. Script formatting and
cross-language rename remain pending.
Typed dialogue context: declare `Dialogue.context({facts = Save.shape(Save.record({...})),
locals = Save.shape(Save.record({...}))})` in a definitions-only Tua module. Save.shape
is a headless schema validator/copier with typed defaults; no save slot or LÖVE required.
A script binds it before labels with `@context "story.context"` and
`@bind name context.player.name`; locals use `@bind visits locals.visits`.
Optional paths require a compatible scalar `default "fallback"`. Paths are data reads,
not arbitrary expressions. Every placeholder in a bound script needs a scalar binding.
Create through `context.new(scene, facts, options?)`, not Dialogue.new. Re-exports retain types.
`getContext()`/`getLocals()` return owned Readonly views. `updateContext(facts)` and
`setLocals(locals)` validate complete replacements and refresh without replaying events.
start resets locals to captured defaults but retains current facts; loops retain both;
cancel retains inspection data; dispose releases it. Players never share mutable locals.
Bindings cannot be overridden by options.args. Custom resolvers return final formatted text.
Context-bound assets emit schemaVersion 2 (header remains @dialogue 1); runtime accepts old schemas.
Use direct built-in factory calls; generic factory wrappers can lose specialized inference.
Conditional dialogue (schema 3): a branch-only label contains
`@branch context.coins >= 20 [target:yes] [else:no]`. Field reads, scalars, nil,
not/and/or, equality and numeric ordering are supported; no calls or arithmetic.
Precedence: parentheses, not, comparisons, and, or. Boolean operators short-circuit;
nil is false and missing ordered operands produce false. Wrong types/paths are errors.
After a choice, `@visible condition` hides it; `@enabled condition` disables it.
`// @id reason.key` followed by `@reason Text` supplies an optional localized reason.
Conditional choice groups require `@fallback label`, used if no visible enabled reply
remains. Snapshot options omit hidden replies; only enabled=false means disabled for
compatibility with older schemas. choose(id) rechecks current accepted context.
Context refresh preserves execution identity unless it follows a no-choice fallback.
Options transitionBudget defaults to 256 (range 1..4096). Budget exhaustion produces
state=faulted and snapshot.issue={code="transition_budget_exceeded",message,nodeId}.
Faulted players do no automatic work; start/cancel/dispose provide explicit recovery.
Conditions have a fixed 32-level/256-instruction runtime limit. Gameplay effects remain host-owned.
Identified timed events: `@event shown 0 pulse [id:arrival.pulse] "soft"` requires
`@document arrival`; event IDs are document-unique and independent of text IDs.
These assets emit schema 4; earlier schemas remain supported. Fired records add
optional eventId, documentId and source={line,column}; legacy records stay unchanged.
Source coordinates are diagnostic only. Explicit IDs survive text edits/reordering;
generation/visit remain per-player delivery tokens, not persisted exactly-once guarantees.
Programmatic events use id and optional source on schema-4 documents with documentId.
Typed dialogue notifications (schema 5): export `Dialogue.events({reward =
Save.shape(Save.record({coins=Save.number(0)}))})`. Before labels declare
`@events "events"`; schedule `@emit shown 0 reward [id:reward.one] {"coins":10}`.
An explicit event/document ID is required. JSON records contain data only; null,
duplicate keys, >8 KiB, >16 nesting levels or >256 values are rejected. Optional
fields are omitted. Imported names/fields/types are checked; numeric bounds are
validated by the captured shape at player construction. Registries have 1–128 names.
Create with events.new(scene); typed notifications have kind=name and owned record
payloads. Use events.read.reward(event) -> payload|nil for typed field access;
tag tests do not currently narrow sibling payload fields. Readers validate/copy a
matching payload. Legacy @event keeps a string payload and no kind. Both count
against 64 events/line. Context composition passes the same registry to
Dialogue.context({facts,locals,events=events}); use context.new(scene,facts).
Payloads are captured on construction. No bus, handlers, action outcomes or save
persistence are implied. Plain Dialogue.new rejects a registry-bound document.
Optional character `portrait: string?` is copied into the line snapshot; hosts load/render it.
After an utterance, `@event shown 0.2 event.name "payload"` or
`@event revealed 0.2 event.name` schedules named data (up to 64 per line).
`player:update(dt, fullyRevealed)` returns due events with name/payload/generation/visit/nodeId.
The first true reveal sample starts that clock at zero; advancing/cancelling discards pending events.
`@timing hold 3 fade 0.35` supplies optional host presentation hints, never automatic advancement.
See docs/dialogue.md for the supported authoring grammar; do not invent commands.

Dialogue.actions({name={payload=Save.shape(...), effect="presentation"|"consequential"}})
registers host actions. Import with @actions "module"; author an action-only
label with @action name [id:stable.id] [success:label] [failure:label] JSON-record.
Use registry.new(source,{handlers={name=function(payload,request) return boolean end}}),
or include actions in Dialogue.context and pass handlers in context.new's options.
Flow waits in awaiting_action until explicit player:runAction(); true/false handler
results select targets. Missing/throwing/invalid handlers fault with source identity;
cancel/start/dispose invalidate reentrant results. Requires dialogue schema 6.
A handler may return a fresh Dialogue.actionHandle({cancel=function() ... end}).
The options record is optional. Handle resolve(boolean), reject(message) and cancel()
settle once; subsequent calls return false (invalid arguments still error).
resolve chooses a branch; reject/cancel fault when consumed. A handle belongs to one
visit only. runAction accepts it with true, returns false while pending, and consumes
settlement on a later call; callbacks/update never advance the player. Even immediate
settlement yields until the next runAction. snapshot().action.status exposes ready,
pending, resolved, rejected or cancelled. handle:snapshot() exposes status and optional
cancellationError. Reject messages and cancellation errors are bounded to 4096 bytes.
Lifecycle invalidation precedes cleanup, contains cleanup errors, and drops late results.
Host work/timeout/rollback remain host-owned; no automatic retries, checkpoints, coroutine dispatch or exactly-once guarantees.

Character expressions (schema 7): exported character records may declare
expressions={happy={portrait="asset-id", animation="optional-host-animation"}}.
After an imported-character utterance, before choices, @expression happy selects
one declared record. Completion/hover/declaration navigation reuse character import
facts. The snapshot node exposes expression, resolved portrait, portraitAnimation.
Omission resets each line to the character's portrait or nil; selection never leaks
across lines/speakers/players. Unknown names fail analysis or dynamic construction.
Selected strings are copied at player construction. Hosts own loading/layout and
one spriteSheet player per presentation; shared cast records contain no playback
state. Asset/animation strings do not execute code or load images during analysis.

Optional dialogue reveal: Dialogue.reveal({rate=30,speech=false,minCueInterval=0.05,
reducedMotion=false}) creates one presentation controller per dialogue player.
Call present(player:snapshot()), update(dt), then player:update(dt,view.complete).
finish() reveals silently and invalidates older cues; report player:update(0,true).
clear() releases text. snapshot() returns text/visible/total/complete/cues plus identity.
clusters() returns owned Unicode 15.1 extended graphemes with inclusive one-based
UTF-8 startByte/endByte. Valid UTF-8 is required, maximum 65536 bytes; rate is (0,1000].
Speech is opt-in: at most one eligible letter/number cluster per update, with a minimum
interval; excess cues are dropped. Whitespace/punctuation are silent. Cue instance,
sequence and dialogue generation/visit/presentationRevision reject stale playback.
Completed locale/context refresh and reduced motion reveal silently. No audio, automatic
advancement, word segmentation, shaping, bidi layout, markup or checkpoints are implied.
Styled spans and authored pause/speed syntax use schema 8; audio profiles remain M7.

Rich dialogue runtime: schema 8 typed line records may include `richText` (raw template)
alongside an exactly matching mark-free `text` fallback template. Choices accept richText;
disabled reasons accept richReason. Tags: em, style=identifier, speed=decimal,
pause=decimal, pronounce="hint"; strict nesting, no code execution, literal args.
`node.presentation` exposes final text, grapheme-indexed runs, boundary pauses,
UTF-8 origin ranges, optional resolvedLocale/variant. Dialogue.reveal consumes runs/pauses;
finish and reducedMotion skip pauses without speech bursts. Template/refresh failures
are atomic. In .tdialogue, place @text rich immediately after @dialogue 1, before
imports/labels/text IDs (blank lines/comments allowed). This emits schema 8 with
raw richText/richReason and plain fallbacks. Timing marks are line-only.
Mark-name completion, hover and static catalog checks share core rich-text rules.
Dialogue extraction retains raw text and adds format="rich" plus plainTemplate.

Dialogue waits: @wait seconds [target:label] occupies its own label and emits schema 9.
Duration is finite, 0..86400. Typed node: {kind="wait",duration=number,next=label}.
Snapshot state is waiting, node absent, wait={duration,elapsed,remaining,source?}.
update(dt,revealed) uses dialogue time, completes at most one wait, discards excess dt;
zero waits still need an update. Errors fault once with wait_transition_error.
player:suspend()/resume() return whether suspension changed. snapshot.suspended is
boolean; state/visit/generation remain unchanged. Suspended updates freeze clocks/events;
advance/choose/runAction return false. Resume does not dispatch actions or catch up wall time. Context refresh defers empty-choice
fallbacks while suspended; resume reconciles them with the transition budget. Resolver
failure on resume throws and preserves suspended choice state for explicit retry.
Host actions may settle while suspended; results are consumed only by later runAction.
A handler that suspends then returns boolean queues its result. Start/cancel/dispose
clear suspension; cancellation/disposal still invalidate pending handles.
Pass snapshots to Dialogue.reveal: present tracks suspension, freezes fractional
reveal/timing and invalidates stale cue sequences. Missing suspended means false for
older snapshots. finish can reveal silently but cannot navigate. Host audio pause,
non-cancellable skip policy and checkpointing remain host responsibilities/future work.

Dialogue audio metadata (schema 10): Dialogue.speechProfile takes/returns a typed,
owned record: sampleSet string (1..256 bytes), pitchMin/pitchMax ordered in [0.25,4],
variation/gain in [0,1], minCueInterval in [0,60], cadence="character"|"word".
Shared character exports may contain speech=profile. After an utterance, before
choices, @speech character selects the imported character's required profile;
@speech off means explicit chatter silence; @speech JSON-record overrides it.
@voice {"cue":"id","sourceLocale":"en","fallback":"silent"|"source","mixSpeech":false}
is optional line metadata. cue is 1..256 bytes, sourceLocale 1..64; no ASCII controls.
Duplicate directives, unknown fields, invalid ranges and duplicate JSON keys fail.
Typed line speech is profile|"off"; voice is the descriptor. Omission resets each line.
Snapshot node.voice adds locale=player locale or sourceLocale and defaults mixSpeech=false.
Voice availability/fallback are host-owned, separate from subtitle fallback: try requested
locale; silent falls back to subtitles, source tries the source recording then silence.
No asset loading, audio playback, synthesis or RNG occurs. Suppress chatter only while
recorded voice plays unless mixSpeech; off always disables chatter, not recorded voice.
Profiles do not configure reveal automatically; its existing cues are grapheme-based.
Word segmentation, profile timing, private RNG, volume, polyphony, audio pause/skip and
lifecycle cleanup belong to the pending host adapter. Pronunciation uses existing rich runs.

Plain dialogue checkpoints: construct with `checkpointVersion` and a document ID,
call `player:checkpoint()` for owned version-1 data and `freshPlayer:restore(data)`
only on a new idle player. Supports line/choice/wait boundaries without context,
registries, branches or conditional choices. Identity/graph/timer validation occurs
before mutation. Restore preserves delivered-event flags and suspension, silently
completes current-line reveal, and exposes snapshot.restored for host audio policy.
Rebind resolvers/args; locale is saved. No filesystem, action dispatch, effect
rollback, partial reveal restoration or exactly-once guarantee is implied.
Typed-context players export version2 with concrete typed, owned locals validated
by Save.shape. Supply current facts to context.new; restore rebinds facts and saves
only locals. Branch/choice conditions, targets, bindings and local defaults enter
the v2 graph signature; v1 plain graphs stay unchanged. Restore never traverses
branches. A saved choice with no enabled visible reply under rebound facts/locals
is rejected without mutation, even with fallback or suspension. Locals are bounded
separately (16384 entries, depth32, 256KiB strings) before schema validation.
Graph identity is not a full schema fingerprint: bump checkpointVersion for
incompatible schema/host semantics. Both versions reject action/event registries.
Shared context definitions retain checkpoint-local types through imports; construct
players in the consumer because additional forwarding of constructed players loses
inference in editor analysis. Action reconciliation and Save recipes remain pending.
Dialogue player options.history = {capacity, maxBytes?} enables optional history.
Capacity is 1..1024; maxBytes is 1..1048576 (default65536 retained string bytes).
player:history() returns owned {entries, capacity, maxBytes, bytes, dropped}.
Entries contain id/kind/nodeId/text and optional documentId/textId/choiceId/speaker/
speakerKey/locale. Lines record full resolved text on entry; accepted choices record
before the destination line. Oldest entries are evicted; oversized entries drop.
Locale/context refreshes preserve original records. No payloads/contexts/media are
retained. redactHistory(id) removes one record; clearHistory() resets entries/counts
without recycling IDs. Cancel/restart retain history; dispose releases it.
Checkpoints exclude history; restore does not append a record. No history import.
